notes:
Lead source: inbound trial signup (dev sandbox). Small B2B SaaS building an in-app chat assistant for customer support and workflow guidance. Team: CTO (ex-frontend), 2 backend, 1 ML engineer. They spun up self-serve account and used free credits to run basic samples. Key quote from CT0: "Priority is perceived snappiness — streaming typing + sub-200ms perceived reply time for short prompts."

Requirements summary:
- Workloads: low-latency chat, streaming responses (SSE/websocket desirable), ephemeral conversational context with short history (max 4 turns).
- Targets: p50 latency < 120ms for model step (client-side target ~200ms end-to-end), p95 < 400ms during normal load. Throughput modest: ~20 concurrent users per region initially, growth plan to 200 concurrent in 6 months.
- Cost sensitivity: Startups budget-conscious — want hosted API price predictability and tooling to understand per-message token costs. Interested in Optimize suggestions (batching/cache) but want pay-as-you-go.
- Model preferences: Prefer open or Redwood-curated small/medium LLMs (efficient 7B–13B class) with streaming tokens; willing to evaluate Redwood-verified profiles.
- Routing/fallback: Need automatic fallback to lighter model when latency spikes; region routing for NA (primary) and EU later.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 baseline, SSO for admin UX, audit logs for support interactions. No on-prem/VPC required today.

Notes from demo and call:
- 2026-02-24 demo: Maya + Daniel ran walkthrough of hosted API streaming endpoints and sample React chat widget. Customer confirmed front-end uses websockets, prefers a streaming SDK over polling.
- 2026-02-28 trial usage: devs tested 2 models (small/medium) with sample dataset; saw average token cost concerns on 2K-10K monthly active messages.
- 2026-03-01 call (Fireflies ff_20260301_00123): CTO asked about token accounting per streaming chunk and ability to limit generation length server-side.

POC idea discussed:
- 2-week POC: integrate hosted API streaming into existing React widget, run 10k messages, measure p50/p95 latency, and track token spend. Redwood to provide recommended batching and cache settings and a pre-built streaming example.

Customer sentiment: positive — "We can get started self-serve but need a short path to measurement and fallback behavior if latency spikes."

Staging notes for AE/SE:
- Provide quickstart: streaming JS sample, recommended throughput config, cost-estimate template (per 1k messages).
- Ask for a small perf trace from their frontend to validate end-to-end latency assumptions.

CRM shorthand and next actions:

- 03/11: tech deep-dive (Daniel) — confirm.
